ety.text: Extracted from отвори́ть (otvorítʹ, “to open”), originally от- (ot-) + -вори́ть (-vorítʹ), later reanalyzed as о- (o-) + -твори́ть (-tvorítʹ), based on a no-longer-existing verb (compare Lithuanian vérti (“to open, to close”) (first singular veriù). More distantly cognate with Latin aperiō (“to open”), operiō (“to close”).

From Medieval Greek ἀλφάβητον (alphábēton). The pronunciation with stress on the second syllable comes directly from the Greek, while the pronunciation with stress on the third syllable was altered, possibly by analogy to French, and gained prestige. Compare Ukrainian алфа́віт (alfávit).
